Medicaid managed care enrollees have a right under 42 CFR §438.10 and 438.404 to receive the specific rules, benefit denial reasons, and criteria the plan used, free of charge. 3) Separately, Florida's overarching Medicaid orthopedic coverage rule (Fla. Admin. Code R. 59G-4.211, 'Orthopedic Services Coverage Policy,' AHCA, last version reviewed dated June 2016, https://flrules.org/gateway/readRefFile.asp?refId=6788&filename=59G-4.211+Orthopedic+Services+Coverage+Policy.pdf) sets only general Florida Medicaid medical-necessity and documentation standards; it does not itemize a conservative-treatment-trial requirement for knee arthroplasty, so it cannot by itself be the 'applicable medical policy' cited in the denial. 4) If the plan cites a licensed clinical criteria set (commonly MCG Care Guidelines or InterQual Procedures — Knee Arthroplasty) rather than an original policy document, the plan is still required to disclose the specific criterion applied to this member upon request (42 CFR §438.210(b)(2)(ii); §438.404(b)(2)).
